evidence: Compared DRAFT.txt with SOURCE.txt word by word, then read the draft in CONTEXT.txt (it appears once, verbatim, as the first three sentences of the second paragraph, after the list of what hypnotism can happen through and before the OECD sentence). SENTENCE 2, 'Marketers and interface designers know this perfectly well.', is identical to his, as the_change says. SENTENCE 1: 'Even when not actively engaging the conscious mind, there are many ways to influence people.' became 'There are a lot of ways to influence people without engaging their conscious mind.' Same claim, and the same point as his published 'Influence doesn't wait for the conscious mind to sign a form.' Differences found: 'many' to 'a lot of' (register only, fits his casual voice); 'the conscious mind' to 'their conscious mind' (their = the people named earlier in the same sentence, so no person is added and 'this' in his next sentence still points at the same thing); the hedge 'actively' is dropped, a very slight sharpening of 'not actively engaging' to 'without engaging'. I judge that immaterial: 'engaging the conscious mind' reads as appealing to conscious judgment, and his published line is at least as strong. No number, condition or person added. SENTENCE 3: 'In the Federal Trade Commission's report on "dark patterns," they describe designs that trick or manipulate consumers.' became 'The Federal Trade Commission has a report on “dark patterns” - designs that trick or manipulate consumers.' The put-back the_change claims is there: 'designs that trick or manipulate consumers' is word for word his, and the three first-draft failures it names ('their', 'used to', 'trick and manipulate') are all absent from this sentence ('or' not 'and', 'that' not 'used to', no possessive before 'consumers'). The one shift is that the verb 'describe' becomes an apposition (the dash defines dark patterns as designs that trick or manipulate consumers instead of saying the report describes them). It is the same fact and each wording entails the other in this context (a report on X describes X), nothing is added, and C04 is clear because the FTC report and what it covers are his published line. TELL ROWS: went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the literal draft in context and found none PRESENT. Weighed specifically: T13 and T09 (the D9 note): his own second sentence is a real aside (the people who profit from this already know it) and the FTC sentence adds a concrete pointer, so the passage does not just fill slots; T19 and T11 (sentence 1 could be read as an announcing opener or a bridge, but it generalizes the list before it and his 'this' depends on it, and no list follows it); T25 (the dash sets off a true appositive that defines the quoted term, not a reveal); T26 ('manipulate' recurs in the OECD sentence, but both are his published words and the repeat shows two bodies saying the same); T12 (the FTC/OECD pairing and 'trick or manipulate' are his); T15 (structure changes and the words are plain, no less-likely swaps); T16 to T18, T20 to T24, T27 to T29 and C01 to C03 have nothing to match. LINTER FINDINGS: (1) 'D9 follows the source order' accepted: the passage follows the words it replaces because it is a sentence-by-sentence rewrite of them, and the place where something is noticed (his aside) is kept. (2) 'E186 without ...ing' accepted: the construction is the claim itself (influence that bypasses the conscious mind); cutting it would lose his meaning, and 'say what happens instead' would add a claim the source does not make; the paragraph before already lists what the influence works through (music, marketing, grief and so on), and the words it replaces had the same negative shape ('not actively engaging'). Residual risk only: one 'without ...ing' remains in the changed text, which is a detector question and not a preservation one. Nothing added, nothing of his left out that the change says it puts back, no change in who does what beyond the describe-to-apposition shift noted above. PASS.
